title: The Strange Mr. Gregory

evidence.note: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips 1972 volume: 'THE STRANGE MR. GREGORY, a photoplay in 7 reels by Monogram Pictures Corp. (C) 14Nov45; L57. United Artists Television, Inc. (PWH)', with a November 1972 renewal registration. The renewal fell within the 28th-year window, so the 1945 copyright was renewed.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Third Series, Vol. 26, Motion Pictures and Filmstrips, 1972 (archive.org)

evidence.note: This is a sound film. The recorded soundtrack was part of the renewed photoplay registration, so it normally shares the film's status. I did not confirm who composed the music or whether any cue has separate music-publisher rights.

editorial:
The Strange Mr. Gregory is a 1945 Monogram Pictures feature, seven reels, directed by Phil Rosen. Monogram registered it for copyright on 14 November 1945. Internet Archive hosts a copy, so a creator may find it easy to locate.

The copyright was renewed, so the film is not free to reuse as a public-domain work. The 1972 Catalog of Copyright Entries lists a renewal filed in the name of United Artists Television, Inc. That puts the renewal in the 28th year, as required. A renewed 1945 work is protected for 95 years from publication, to the end of 2040. Being on a streaming site or an archive does not change that. Clear it with the current rights holder, or wait for the term to expire.
faq: Is The Strange Mr. Gregory in the public domain?

Not on the evidence I found. The 1972 Catalog of Copyright Entries lists a renewal of the November 1945 registration, filed by United Artists Television, Inc. A renewed 1945 film is still under copyright, whatever the websites that host it say.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy in my project?

Do not assume so. Internet Archive hosting does not clear rights, and the film's copyright was renewed. Get permission from the current rights holder before commercial or public use. A short excerpt might qualify as fair use, but that is a case-by-case question.
